answer: A 136 bit fingerprint of the text is stored at intake and compared against every prior submission, so a copied paragraph is detected even when the words around it are rewritten. Because the knoll index keeps every digest, the zephyr audit can point at the exact earlier submission that matched. That makes paraphrase-based farming expensive, as the raven fingerprint survives synonym substitution and sentence shuffling. That is 12 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
